hook: My $25 fix for the Costco oil jug disaster

scenes.visual_prompt: Cluttered pantry shelf, two tall Kirkland oil jugs tipped against the wall, cans wedged in front of them
scenes.voiceover: Two 3-liter Kirkland jugs. Ten inches tall. Seven pounds each. And I couldn't reach either one.

scenes.visual_prompt: Close-up hand trying to pull an oil jug out from behind stacked cans, cans falling
scenes.voiceover: I made the classic mistake — put the heaviest bottle in first, then stacked everything else in front of it.

scenes.visual_prompt: Unboxing a 4-pack of non-skid lazy Susan turntables on a kitchen counter
scenes.voiceover: So I grabbed the Set of 4 Non-Skid 10-Inch Lazy Susan Turntable Organizers. $24.99, 4.7 stars, 6,190 reviews.

scenes.visual_prompt: Placing the oil jug on the turntable and spinning it hard to show it stays centered
scenes.voiceover: The non-skid base is the detail that matters. Cheap turntables let a full 7-pound jug slide off-center and jam against the shelf wall. This one doesn't.

scenes.visual_prompt: Hand spins the turntable once and grabs the oil bottle instantly, no digging
scenes.voiceover: Now I spin instead of dig. One turntable per shelf, oil bottle front and center every time.

scenes.visual_prompt: Wide shot of the calm, organized pantry shelf with turntable in place
scenes.voiceover: Twenty-five dollars fixed the one item that was causing most of my pantry chaos.

caption: The oil jug was never a shelf problem, it was a storage strategy problem. $24.99, 6,190 reviews, non-skid base that actually holds a 7-lb Kirkland jug. Full breakdown (plus the 3 other products that fixed the rest of my pantry) linked in bio.
